solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Saintly name taken by groom at the wedding

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the run of words groom at the wedding, taken by them as a container would take them

explanation.surface: A bridegroom adopts a saint's name on his wedding day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a solver to think about the groom's own name; the name actually sits across groOM AT THE Wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Matthew is the apostle and evangelist, so his name is a saintly one.

clue.text: A dog's dinner can be what Tommy has for his meal!

definitions.text: what Tommy has for his meal

parts.note: a dog's dinner is British slang for a mess
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A shambles can be a soldier's supper.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is Tommy Atkins, the nickname for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers eat from a small metal cooking and eating container issued as field kit.

clue.text: Tailless flatfish needs support like some jet aircraft

indicators.note: tailless means the fish loses its final letter

parts.note: a turbot is a flatfish
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A flatfish without its tail needs propping up, like a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: like some jet aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes aircraft powered by a jet turbine driving a propeller.

clue.text: He is briefly in possession of the Spanish lists

indicators.note: in possession of means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: he is shortened to he's
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: He holds the Spanish lists.
explanation.walkthrough: Lists is a verb: a ship that lists tilts to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels leans over to one side, which is to say it lists.

clue.text: A layer of dust

parts.note: read not as a film of dust but as something that lays dust, damping down a road

explanation.walkthrough: Layer is one who lays: a cart that sprays water on dusty roads lays the dust.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon carrying water was used to spray unpaved streets and keep the dust down.

clue.text: A little European, seen as future prince in fairy tale

parts.note: a tad is a small amount, a little
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A small European is cast as a prince-to-be in a fairy story.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Frog Prince the prince is a frog, so the creature that will become a frog is the prince's future self.
explanation.definitionFit: A frog's larva grows into a frog, and the fairy-tale frog becomes a prince, so it is a future prince.

clue.text: Fashion starts to turn ridiculous on purpose

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Fashion begins to turn silly deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a current style or fashion.

clue.text: Parties without doubt work miracles

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the parties wrap round the other word

parts.note: dos are parties
to wonder is to doubt

explanation.surface: Undoubtedly parties achieve wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve remarkable results is idiomatically to perform marvels.

clue.text: One who has depression takes day off

indicators.note: off means the day letter is taken away from the depression word

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience or depressed mood

explanation.surface: A depressed person takes a day off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who possesses something is its proprietor.

clue.text: A dish and spoon in nursery rhyme, say

definitions.text: A dish and spoon in nursery rhyme, say

parts.words: A dish and spoon in nursery rhyme, say
parts.note: in Hey Diddle Diddle the dish ran away with the spoon, a pair running off together

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme ends 'the dish ran away with the spoon', a runaway couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run off secretly to marry are runaways, like the dish and spoon.

clue.text: Soldier perhaps leaves NCO some material

indicators.note: leaves means the soldier departs from the rank of NCO, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer
a soldier ant is one kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier quits his sergeant, leaving some cloth behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' reads as a military man but is the soldier ant, a caste of ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Weak do not train for this Olympic event

indicators.note: to train is to put into shape by drilling, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Feeble people are advised not to train for this Olympic sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' sits as the verb of the advice, but it is the anagram signal for WEAK DO NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This Korean martial art of kicks and punches has been an Olympic sport since 2000.

clue.text: Pocketed money (undeserved) — sure to upset a socialist

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Undeserved cash taken in is certain to anger a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocketed' suggests a past-tense verb, and it is: British slang for taking money, here undeservedly. 'upset' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to trouser money is to pocket it, often money one has not earned.

clue.text: Old Scandinavian doctor wants only half of course

parts.note: Dr No is the villainous doctor of the first Bond film, so doctor gives his surname

indicators.note: only half of tells us to keep just one half of the word course, here its back three letters

explanation.surface: An old Norseman's physician needs only half a course of treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr No is the Bond film villain, giving NO; the back half of COURSE is RSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The language and people of medieval Scandinavia are called by this name, as in Old Norse.

clue.text: Sauce bottle

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: A bottle of sauce on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like the kitchen, but sauce is cheek and bottle is courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Effrontery, cheek, is one meaning; steady courage, pluck, is another sense of the same word.

clue.text: Two-man contribution to a bygone age — the noughties?

definitions.text: Two-man contribution to a bygone age — the noughties?

parts.words: Two-man contribution to a bygone age — the noughties?
parts.note: two men's names, Edward and Ian, join to name the era of the 1900s, the first decade of the twentieth century

explanation.walkthrough: The 1901–10 reign of Edward VII was the first decade of the century, its own noughties; the word also splits into two men's names.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of King Edward VII, 1901 to 1910, is named after him.

clue.text: Starlets in Hair start with a big number

indicators.note: start with says the hair word is preceded by the other pieces

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Young stars in the musical Hair begin with a big show-stopping number.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair looks like the title of the rock musical but it simply means tresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlets are young female film performers hoping to become stars.

clue.text: A saint worried about success for an island people

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the other piece
worried means shaken about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: An anxious saint about to succeed among an island people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' gives the anagram TAIANS from A SAINT; 'about' puts it round the success word.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of a South Pacific island in French Polynesia are a people of an island.

clue.text: Alter stem to create smaller flower

indicators.note: to create means to make something new from the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Change a stem to make a smaller bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is something that flows, a river, not a bloom; 'Alter' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brook is a lesser watercourse, and anything that flows is a flower in crossword terms.

clue.text: Uses ducking stool? This could lower the beam

definitions.meaning: read as two words, plunges a sorceress into water, as the ducking stool was used for
a car's headlight control that dips the beam for oncoming drivers

explanation.surface: Old punishment of suspected sorceresses beside a car's headlamp control.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: split the answer as DIPS WITCH, which is what a ducking stool was for.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipswitch is the car control that lowers headlamps from main beam to dipped.

clue.text: "Exit, exit!" Light Brigade's fatal order, effectively

parts.note: a door is an exit
to exit is to die

explanation.surface: A cry of 'Get out, get out!' as the Light Brigade's deadly order.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson wrote of the Light Brigade: 'Theirs but to do and die'; the order in effect demanded this.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a desperate all-or-nothing order, which is what the Charge of the Light Brigade amounted to.

clue.text: Reverse roles as a form of punishment

indicators.note: reverse tells us to read the word for roles from back to front

parts.note: an actor's roles are parts

explanation.surface: Swapping roles as a way of disciplining someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating with a leather belt, the strap, was a common form of corporal punishment.

clue.text: Kind of bear is seen only after dark

parts.note: a polar bear is a kind of bear

explanation.surface: A type of bear that is only seen at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pole Star, Polaris, is a star visible only at night.

clue.text: Senior shows more daring sacrificing bishop

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving up, as a chess player gives up a bishop, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: bolder means more daring
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: An elderly chess player plays more boldly by sacrificing a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone senior is older in age or higher in rank.

clue.text: Newspaper to follow central guideline in China

indicators.note: to follow means the newspaper comes after the other piece
central means the middle letters of guideline

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A newspaper following a central guideline on China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is tableware, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is tin-glazed earthenware from the Dutch town, a kind of china.

clue.text: Where climbers may go mad

definitions.meaning: climbing plants grow on a vertical surface
British idiom for being driven to fury or madness

explanation.surface: A place where mountaineers might go crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Climbers are plants such as ivy, not mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving someone up the wall is an idiom for making them furious or crazy.

clue.text: Old city atlas oddly depicting these mountains

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of atlas are kept

explanation.surface: An old city atlas strangely shows these mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain range dividing Europe from Asia is a set of mountains.

clue.text: Dread getting guillotined by mistake

indicators.note: getting guillotined means losing the head, the first letter

parts.note: terror is dread

explanation.surface: Dread of being beheaded by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The guillotine nods to the Reign of Terror of the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Young man returns (with first-class City degree) to be religious leader

indicators.note: returns means the word for a young man is read back the other way

parts.note: a lad is a young man
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
LA is Los Angeles, the city
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A young man comes back with a first and a City degree to become a religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: City reads as London's financial district but is LA.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism holds this title.

clue.text: The measure of a king

definitions.meaning: a straight-edged measuring stick marked in inches or centimetres
a king is a sovereign who governs

explanation.surface: Taking the measure of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a measuring stick and a sovereign, such as a king.

clue.text: Areas where No 10 (twice!) gets caught with wrong set

indicators.note: gets caught with means the numbers are held inside the jumbled letters
wrong means the letters of set are put in the wrong order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
the number ten given a second time, now in words

explanation.surface: Downing Street, twice over, is caught with the wrong crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 suggests Downing Street, but it is simply ten, given once as a numeral and once in words. 'wrong' makes ETS from SET, which 'gets caught with' wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The extent of something is its size or area, so extents are areas covered.

clue.text: Special ceremonies of goblins,elves and imps

parts.note: rites are religious or solemn ceremonies

explanation.surface: Special rituals performed by goblins, elves and imps.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are fairies or mischievous little supernatural beings, the same family as goblins and imps.
